searchText: <@!689161464829050960> It seems like the `Frontier` version of the YP has it named as `SUICIDE`. It was aliased as `SELFDESTRUCT` in `EIP-6` and that can be seen in all versions of the YP starting from `Homestead`. Question: Do we want to rename it to `SELFDESTRUCT` in the `Frontier` version itself `OR` do we want to preserve the history by naming it `SUICIDE` in the `Frontier` version and then rename in the later forks? My personal preference is to preserve history and see the changes through the diff that will be generated between forks. I've kinda imagined two classes of EIPs: - Ones that apply from a hardfork forward (like changing the gas price of an opcode); and - Ones that apply to all hardforks retroactively (like putting a cap on the size of RLP-encoded integers) Since there are no consensus changes for renaming `SUICIDE` (it's all documentation), I think we should rename it in all forks. That said, if we want to be _truly_ pedantic, we should go with `SUICIDE` until we officially implement EIP-6 and only then rename it in all forks. > Ones that apply to all hardforks retroactively (like putting a cap on the size of RLP-encoded integers) Might be slightly OT, but any idea why `SUICIDE` has not been renamed in the frontier version of the YP? Does the yellowpaper maintain active branches for different hard forks? I've never looked ^^;; Yes it does. I compiled different fork branches earlier today before commenting. That's a great question then. I think only master is maintained.
